records.title: Molecular mechanisms and targeted therapeutic strategies for glycolytic reprogramming in osteosarcoma.
records.abstract: Osteosarcoma, a highly invasive and metastatic malignant bone tumor, has a poor prognosis primarily because of early pulmonary metastasis and resistance to conventional treatments. The malignant progression of osteosarcoma cells significantly depends on glycometabolic reprogramming, a process characterized by enhanced aerobic glycolysis. This review begins by mapping the multi-dimensional networks driving sugar metabolism reprogramming, which revealed that functional abnormalities in core glycolytic enzymes, including hexokinase 2, pyruvate kinase M2, and lactate dehydrogenase A (LDHA), are driven by a multi-level regulatory network that includes altered transcription factor activity, epigenetic modifications, and interactions mediated by non-coding RNAs. Mitochondrial dysfunction leads to succinate and reactive oxygen species accumulation, synergistically promoting the remodeling of metabolic pathways. Furthermore, the synergistic interaction between the pentose phosphate pathway and glutamine metabolism accelerates the energy supply and biosynthesis, whereas lactate accumulation shapes the immunosuppressive microenvironment by inhibiting immune cell function. This review focuses on dissecting the core mechanisms of glucose metabolism reprogramming in osteosarcoma pathogenesis, including promoting proliferation, inhibiting apoptosis, enhancing invasion and metastasis, regulating immune metabolism, and mediating chemotherapy resistance. Additionally, it evaluates novel therapeutic strategies targeting key nodes of glucose metabolism in osteosarcoma, including advances in preclinical research on specific small-molecule inhibitors and gene regulatory approaches. Finally, it delves into the major challenges in translational research, such as metabolic heterogeneity, targeting selectivity, and compensatory resistance, as well as prospects for future research, including multi-omics analysis, smart delivery systems, organoid models, and combination immunotherapy. This study offers novel insights into overcoming the therapeutic bottlenecks in osteosarcoma treatment.

records.title: A review of advances in research on mechanisms inhibiting kidney stone formation from a network pharmacology perspective.
records.abstract: Nephrolithiasis is a prevalent, highly recurrent urological disorder affecting 1%-15% of the global population, with 5-year recurrence rates reaching up to 50%. While surgical interventions achieve acute stone clearance, they do not resolve underlying metabolic derangements, crystal-induced tubular injury, or chronic inflammatory cascades. Natural products from global ethnomedicinal systems (including Traditional Chinese Medicine, Indian Ayurveda, Persian Unani medicine, European phytotherapy, and African ethnopharmacology) demonstrate potent multi-target anti-urolithic properties. However, decoding their intricate polypharmacology remains a major challenge. Network pharmacology, combining multi-omics profiling, computational target prediction, and network topology, has emerged as a promising paradigm to decipher these multi-component mechanisms. Unlike previous descriptive reviews that largely focused on narrow botanical catalogs or local traditions, this review establishes a critical, globally inclusive, and methodologically rigorous synthesis of network pharmacology-driven nephrolithiasis research from 2022 to 2026. We detail the fundamental pathophysiology across major stone types (calcium oxalate, calcium phosphate, uric acid, struvite, cystine) and the comprehensive cellular cascade encompassing crystal nucleation, Randall's plaque/plug formation, CD44-mediated adhesion, mitochondrial reactive oxygen species burst, endoplasmic reticulum stress, NLRP3 inflammasome activation, macrophage M1/M2 polarization, immunometabolism, extracellular vesicle communication, and programmed cell death (apoptosis, necroptosis, pyroptosis, ferroptosis, and PANoptosis). We critically synthesize evidence across diverse chemical classes (flavonoids, polyphenols, pentacyclic triterpenes, alkaloids, anthraquinones, tannins, polysaccharides, and marine bioactive metabolites), bridging computational predictions with established mechanistic milestones. Furthermore, we provide a deep critical appraisal of core methodological bottlenecks-target prediction bias, publication bias of over-studied hub genes, arbitrary pharmacokinetic cutoffs, circular virtual docking, and lack of renal bioavailability validation. Finally, we formulate a forward-looking translational roadmap integrating single-cell transcriptomics, humanized 3D organoid co-cultures, spatial multi-omics, reverse validation in longitudinal clinical registries, and machine learning feature selection, providing rigorous guidance for precision anti-urolithic drug discovery.

records.title: Phospholipid codes at virus-host membrane interfaces: mechanisms and therapeutic opportunities in animal viral diseases.
records.abstract: Animal viruses depend on host membranes at every stage of infection, yet membrane lipid states are often treated as background rather than as causal determinants of virus-host interactions. This Review develops a phospholipid-code framework in which headgroup identity, acyl-chain chemistry, leaflet topology, and lipid flux define infection-stage-specific membrane states. Evidence from Newcastle disease virus, infectious bronchitis virus, avian influenza virus, porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus, African swine fever virus, Senecavirus A, Japanese encephalitis virus, and porcine epidemic diarrhea virus shows that these states can control attachment, endosomal progression, growth of replication organelles, viral protein allostery, budding, virion infectivity, ferroptotic tissue injury, and delivery of vaccines or antivirals. Comparative evidence from human and plant virus systems is used only to identify transferable membrane mechanisms that require validation in animal-virus models and natural host species. The framework distinguishes viral lipid demand from host defense and tissue damage and explains why total-cell lipidomics or broad metabolic inhibitors rarely establish causality. We argue that the most promising interventions will target viral protein-lipid interfaces, virus-specific recruitment of lipid-transfer machinery, transient leaflet transitions, virion envelopes, or pathological lipid oxidation rather than globally suppressing essential lipid metabolism. Species-relevant primary cells, organoids, virion lipidomics, topology-resolved assays, acute perturbation, rescue experiments, and animal challenge models will be required to translate causal phospholipid biology into safe and practical antiviral strategies for livestock and poultry health.

records.title: Tumor-on-chip and cancer microphysiological platforms: knowledge structure, thematic evolution, and the emergence of organoid-integrated models, 2010-2025.
records.abstract: Cancer microphysiological systems (MPS), including tumor-on-chip platforms, combine engineered microenvironments, controlled fluid transport, and tumor-relevant biological models for cancer modeling, drug testing, and translational research. Organoid-integrated chips represent one developing component within this broader field, but the publication growth, knowledge structure, and changing research priorities of cancer MPS and tumor-on-chip research have not been systematically mapped across major bibliographic databases. We performed a dual-database bibliometric analysis of publications indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus from 2010 to 2025. Bibliometric indicators were analyzed using Bibliometrix, VOSviewer, and CiteSpace. We examined publication growth, source distribution, author and country collaboration, highly cited and co-cited references, and temporal keyword evolution. In addition, a phase-split keyword analysis was conducted to compare the research emphasis during 2010-2020 and 2021-2025. A total of 476 publications were included in the final cancer MPS/tumor-on-chip corpus. Research output increased markedly after 2020 and reached 101 articles in 2025. Source, co-citation, and keyword analyses suggested a progressive shift from early emphasis on microfluidic device construction and physical culture control toward greater attention to biofabrication, tumor microenvironment reconstruction, immune-related interactions, and drug-screening and other application-oriented themes. Phase-split keyword analysis showed that recent publications placed greater attention on biological applications and translational questions while retaining a clear connection with earlier engineering-oriented research. The United States and China emerged as the major research hubs, although with different collaboration profiles. This study provides a dual-database bibliometric analysis of cancer microphysiological systems and tumor-on-chip research from 2010 to 2025. The field has expanded from microfluidic engineering and basic tumor reconstruction toward tumor microenvironment modeling, multicellular interactions, drug-related applications, and organoid integration. These trends indicate growing translational interest, although the biological performance and clinical utility of individual platforms require direct experimental evaluation.

records.title: The ablation margin as a regenerative and immunosuppressive niche in hepatocellular carcinoma: multicellular remodeling and organoid-on-a-chip modeling.
records.abstract: Thermal ablation is an important local treatment for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet post-ablation local tumor progression remains a major obstacle to durable disease control. Traditionally, recurrence has been attributed mainly to incomplete thermal coverage, inadequate ablative margins, or heat-sink effects. However, increasing evidence suggests that the sublethal thermal injury (STI) zone at the ablation margin is not merely a passive physical boundary, but a biologically active injury-repair microenvironment. Within this region, gradients of thermal dose, hypoxia, damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs), extracellular matrix mechanics, and immune infiltration may interact to shape residual tumor cell behavior. Post-ablation remodeling is likely driven by coordinated crosstalk among myeloid cells, hepatic stellate cells/cancer-associated fibroblast-like stromal cells (HSCs/CAFs), endothelial cells, neutrophils, adaptive immune cells, and residual tumor cells. These interactions may promote epithelial-mesenchymal transition, stem-like plasticity, immune evasion, angiogenic repair, and local tumor progression. Current two-dimensional (2D) cultures lack three-dimensional architecture and multicellular spatial interactions, whereas animal models are limited by variable thermal dose control, restricted real-time imaging, and interspecies differences. Emerging HCC organoid-on-a-chip platforms may help address these gaps by integrating patient-derived organoids (PDOs), tunable extracellular matrix hydrogels, microfluidic thermal and hypoxic gradients, and defined multicellular co-culture modules. Importantly, immune checkpoint testing requires immune-competent extensions incorporating autologous T cells, and antigen-presentation studies require dendritic cells. This review discusses the ablation margin as a multicellular recurrence niche and evaluates organoid-on-a-chip systems as hypothesis-generating tools for mechanism-guided and safety-conscious adjuvant strategy development.

records.title: Personalized prediction of sequential therapeutic responses in HR+/HER2-low breast cancer using patient-derived organoids.
records.abstract: The clinically recommended treatment for hormone receptor-positive/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-low (HR+/HER2-low) advanced breast cancer involves endocrine therapy (e.g., fulvestrant) followed by antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) such as trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd; formerly DS-8201) and sacituzumab govitecan (SG). However, the therapeutic outcomes of this sequential regimen remain suboptimal, and direct evidence is lacking as to whether this sequence is optimal. Additionally, the sequence of DS-8201 and SG is also unknown. Patient-derived organoids (PDOs) have emerged as a promising preclinical tool, shown to predict personalized drug responses and correlate well with clinical outcomes. Therefore, using PDOs from HR+/HER2-low breast cancer, this study aims to systematically evaluate the antitumor effects of different administration sequences involving fulvestrant and ADCs (i.e., DS-8201 or SG), as well as DS-8201 and SG and to provide evidence for optimizing treatment sequencing. PDOs were established from fresh breast cancer tissues and characterized by immunohistochemistry (IHC), hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining, and immunofluorescence (IF) to confirm histopathological and phenotypic features fidelity to original tumors. Organoid viability was assessed using the CellTiter-Glo 3D (CTG-3D) assay, and morphological changes were monitored by bright-field microscopy. After treatment with fulvestrant, DS-8201, or SG alone, IHC and IF were performed to detect key proteins involved in the mechanism of action of SG and DS-8201. Our results demonstrated that administering DS-8201 or SG followed by fulvestrant yielded superior antitumor effects compared with the reverse sequence (fulvestrant followed by ADCs). Moreover, organoids revealed marked patient heterogeneity in response to the sequential administration of DS-8201 and SG (i.e., DS-8201 then SG vs. SG then DS-8201). Notably, relying solely on expression levels of biomarkers alone was insufficient to accurately predict ADCs sensitivity in organoids that had received prior therapy. The sequence of DS-8201/SG followed by fulvestrant is a more suitable treatment regimen than the conventional sequence (fulvestrant followed by ADCs) for HR+/HER2-low breast cancer. This study provides important preclinical evidence supporting the optimization of therapy sequences in personalized medicine and advances the application of organoid-based models in oncology research.

records.title: Dynamic Graph Prior-Guided Latent Adaptation for Generalizable Single-Cell Perturbation Response Prediction.
records.abstract: Predicting transcriptional responses to drug perturbations in unseen cellular contexts is a central challenge in single-cell perturbation modeling. This challenge creates a need for models that combine flexible state transitions with structured biological prior knowledge. Existing data-driven models often struggle to generalize across unseen cell types, while many prior-based models rely on static biological graphs without explicitly conditioning prior influence on perturbation-specific target support. We propose DGP-LA, a dynamic graph-prior latent adaptation framework that refines biological priors and injects them as gated latent corrections within a cell-state-conditioned transition model. DGP-LA couples a transition backbone with perturbation-conditioned sparse graph refinement. It propagates gene-aligned target support over the refined graph and selectively injects the resulting topology-aware signal into the hidden representation. On Tahoe and NeurIPS, DGP-LA improves Pearson Delta relative to State by 8.7% and 35.8% for generalization across unseen cell types. In zero-shot drug perturbation response prediction on unseen cell types, it improves Pearson Delta relative to CRISP by 79.1% and 67.6%. The model also improves DE-gene recovery, response discrimination, and Hallmark pathway recovery, supporting adaptive latent integration of biological priors for more generalizable and biologically interpretable perturbation modeling. DGP-LA's source code and reproducibility materials are available at https://github.com/bieyl/DGP-LA and archived on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22155398. Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

records.title: Benchmarking biological knowledge-graph priors against single-cell foundation models for Perturb-seq prediction.
records.abstract: Perturb-seq prediction increasingly relies on either biological graph priors or single-cell foundation models, but their relative value is difficult to interpret when architectures, split definitions and graph sources vary simultaneously. We benchmarked STRING functional associations and Gene Ontology co-annotation against dense, self-edge-only and exact-degree-rewired supports in one fixed graph-attention backbone, with a separate 200-HVG STRING-GO-control-co-expression sensitivity. Four public Perturb-seq datasets, three nested gene-space scales and three optimisation seeds were evaluated on held-out guide conditions; GEARS, scGPT and Geneformer were evaluated on the same held-out conditions, output-gene panels and Pearson-r metric after model-specific validity checks. At 200 highly variable genes, STRING-GO improved the equal-dataset Pearson r by +0.016 (95% interval [+0.010, +0.022]) relative to dense support. Dataset effects were positive in Adamson (+0.017), Norman (+0.015), Replogle K562 (+0.017) and Replogle RPE1 (+0.014), and 122/200 guide conditions improved (0.61 [0.54,0.68]). The top-20-gene Jaccard difference was +0.009 [+0.006,+0.012]. STRING-GO exceeded self-edge-only support by +0.024 [+0.018,+0.029] and the mean of ten exact-degree rewires by +0.011 [+0.005,+0.017]. The native-panel effect declined from +0.016 at 200 genes to +0.009 at 1000 genes; the 1000-200 interaction was -0.006 [-0.011,-0.002]. The primary graph-support comparison was formulated and conducted during peer-review revision rather than planned as an a priori confirmatory study. All three external models passed implementation-specific checks. Across 36 protocol-matched dataset-scale contrasts, 32 were within the descriptive ±0.030 reference envelope and four were outside, all favouring the external model. These results demonstrate a modest empirical predictive improvement under the evaluated matched protocol; they do not by themselves establish practical biological relevance.

records.title: AI-enabled fungal biomanufacturing: from genome mining to the artificial intelligence virtual cell.
records.abstract: Fungi are important chassis organisms for sustainable biomanufacturing owing to their strong secretion capacity, metabolic diversity, and adaptability to industrial processes. Driven by the rapid development of Artificial Intelligence (AI), computational approaches that enable machines to learn patterns from data and make predictions, together with omics technologies and synthetic biology, data- and model-driven strategies are increasingly reshaping fungal cell factory design and optimization. This review summarizes recent advances in AI-enabled fungal biomanufacturing, covering AI-assisted genome mining, enzyme and pathway analysis, genome editing, metabolic network modeling, and intelligent fermentation control. The review further highlights the emerging concept of the artificial intelligence virtual cell (AIVC), which integrates multi-omics data, mechanistic modeling, and machine learning-based approaches into a unified multiscale framework for simulating dynamic cellular behaviors. The technical foundations and potential applications of AIVC in fungal metabolic engineering, drug discovery, agriculture, and environmental biotechnology are reviewed. Finally, key challenges-data quality and standardization, cross-scale model integration and interpretability, and the gap between in silico prediction and experimental validation-are highlighted. This review provides a systematic perspective on the role of AI and virtual cell technologies in advancing next generation fungal biotechnology.

records.title: PHAROS: turning single-cell perturbation models into target-directed drug-combination screens.
records.abstract: Combination therapies are central to cancer treatment, but exhaustive screening is impractical. We introduce PHAROS, a framework that turns a pretrained single-cell perturbation model into a target-directed search engine for drug combinations. PHAROS predicts how a cell population changes under a drug, one drug at a time, then chains these predictions together to simulate drug combinations. It scores each simulated outcome against the desired target state and uses a search algorithm to find the most promising combinations, all without retraining the underlying model. Across two independent combinatorial perturbation datasets, PHAROS recovered exact or mechanism-matched two-drug responses in cell lines, both seen and unseen during model training. Its rankings were specific to the requested conversion and were not explained by single-drug effects, additive effects, or shared mechanism of action. In exploratory analyses of patient-derived metastatic HR+/HER2- breast tumors and basal cell carcinoma (BCC), PHAROS prioritized FDA-approved regimens, distinguished combinations by their predicted tumor-versus-immune objective profiles, and nominated pathway-level hypotheses, while explicitly identifying both tumor cohorts as outside the model's supported distribution. PHAROS provides a modular route from pretrained virtual-cell models to inverse, single-cell combination-screening platforms.

records.title: Pop-Corn: Predicting Perturbation Phenotype Effects Across Single-Cell and Spatial Contexts.
records.abstract: Genetic perturbations can reshape cell populations by altering the relative abundance of specific cell types and states within the profiled population, including increases, decreases and states that become detectable after perturbation. Pooled single-cell screens, such as Perturb-seq, measure such responses at scale. However, only a small fraction of possible perturbations can be tested experimentally. A central challenge is therefore to predict compositional shifts induced by unseen perturbations. Many perturbation-prediction methods do not directly optimize for this outcome; instead, they predict gene-expression responses and infer cell-type and cell-state composition downstream. Surprisingly, we find that even models that accurately predict perturbation-induced changes in average gene expression perform poorly at forecasting these compositional shifts. To address this gap, we present Pop-Corn, a method that directly predicts how a perturbation reshapes cell-type composition without reconstructing gene expression. In the primary T-cell benchmark, Pop-Corn predicted the overall cell-state composition of held-out perturbations more accurately than the evaluated expression-prediction pipelines, while better preserving the diversity of observed cell states. We further extend Pop-Corn to intact tissue, where it predicts perturbation-induced cell-type proportion changes in local cellular neighborhoods and uses attention patterns to generate hypotheses about context-dependent cellular interactions. Retrospective virtual screens support the use of Pop-Corn to prioritize perturbations for experimental follow-up according to their predicted effects on cell-state composition.

records.title: MolecureAI: an agentic AI platform for autonomous drug discovery.
records.abstract: Accelerating the identification of viable drug candidates across therapeutic areas demands autonomous systems for molecular generation that enforce chemical correctness by structural invariants rather than model capability. We present MolecureAI, an autonomous AI agent architecture for closed-loop drug discovery with cost-ordered cascade evaluation that addresses four capability gaps unresolved across the field: autonomous design strategy selection, persistent cross-campaign structural memory, in-loop ADMET safety gating, and literature-scale evidence integration into the generative loop. A cost-ordered cascade concentrates full structure-based evaluation on a small pre-filtered survivor set, achieving a 2.5 × reduction in candidates advanced relative to those generated. An in-loop metabolic gate enforces Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, and Toxicity (ADMET) safety by writing flagged reactive substructures to a per-target learned state, suppressing identified liabilities from all subsequent generation rounds. A persistent campaign memory influences generation trajectories by embedding prior structural success and failure patterns directly into the design context. We validate these architectural invariants across three structurally diverse benchmark targets (EGFR, KRAS G 12 C , and BRD4) through a five-condition component ablation and a controlled memory ablation, and confirm generator agnosticism across four language-model backends via a deterministic recalibration layer that overrides backend self-evaluation bias. Without explicit chemotype instruction, the pipeline computationally converged toward candidates bearing the 4-anilinoquinazoline scaffold characteristic of the approved inhibitors erlotinib and gefitinib, from structural feedback alone. Persistent campaign memory showed directional but non-significant trends toward lower inter-round score variance and higher late-stage advance rate ( n ≈ 90 per condition; all p > 0.20 ). The component ablation reveals that optimizing for a single objective collapses performance on others; only full orchestration resolves this tension. Advancement rates above 79% across all backends confirm that the validated properties are generator-agnostic, enforced by architectural invariants rather than model capability. All reported outcomes are properties of the computational generation process; prospective biochemical validation of the advanced candidates remains the primary direction for future work.

records.title: Functional alignment of protein language models via reinforcement learning.
records.abstract: Protein language models (pLMs) enable generative design of novel protein sequences but remain fundamentally misaligned with protein engineering goals, as they lack explicit understanding of function and often fail to improve properties beyond those found in nature. We introduce Reinforcement Learning from eXperimental Feedback (RLXF), a general framework that aligns protein language models with experimentally measured functional objectives, drawing inspiration from the methods used to align large language models like ChatGPT. Applied across five diverse protein families, RLXF improves generation of high-functioning variants beyond pre-trained baselines. We demonstrate this with CreiLOV, an oxygen-independent fluorescent protein, where RLXF-aligned models generate sequences with significantly enhanced fluorescence, including the most fluorescent CreiLOV variants reported to date. Our results indicate that RLXF-aligned models effectively integrate the evolutionary knowledge encoded in pre-trained pLMs with experimental observations, improving the success rate of generated sequences and enabling the discovery of synergistic mutation combinations that are difficult to identify through zero-shot or evolutionary approaches. RLXF provides a scalable and accessible approach to steer generative models toward desired biochemical properties, enabling function-driven protein design beyond the limits of natural evolution.

records.title: Perspectives on tissue-selective insulin derivatives.
records.abstract: Insulin is a central regulator of metabolic homoeostasis with diverse, tissue-specific actions across multiple organs. Despite major advances in insulin formulations, current therapies rely on systemic delivery and do not reproduce the physiological distribution of endogenous insulin, resulting in non-physiological tissue exposure and associated metabolic limitations. In this perspective, we discuss emerging strategies aimed at achieving tissue-selective insulin action, including molecular engineering of insulin analogues, modulation of insulin receptor isoform specificity and targeted delivery approaches. Attention is given to hepato-preferential, muscle-directed, brain-targeted and adipose-modulating strategies, highlighting their mechanistic basis, therapeutic potential and inherent limitations. While proof of principle has been established for several approaches, challenges remain in balancing tissue selectivity with whole-body metabolic control. Advances in protein design and delivery technologies may ultimately enable the development of next-generation insulin therapies that better mimic physiological insulin action and improve clinical outcomes in metabolic and neurodegenerative diseases.

records.title: Coordinating structure-guided design and cis-regulatory optimization to engineer elite herbicide-tolerance alleles in crops.
records.abstract: Genome editing facilitates the rapid creation of elite alleles, yet identifying editable sites for durable trait improvement without functional trade-offs remains challenging. Most current strategies modify a single genetic axis, limiting their effectiveness and stability. Here we developed a dual-layer allele engineering framework integrating structure-guided protein design with precise cis-regulatory tuning to overcome such constraints. Using rice 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate dioxygenase (OsHPPD) as a model, structural analysis enabled the rational design of coding variants that retain enzymatic activity while conferring herbicide resistance. To further enhance resistance, we introduced a highly efficient 22-bp expression-modulating element into the engineered alleles, generating combinatorial coding and regulatory variants with significantly improved resistance, up to four times the recommended field application rate. Importantly, the dual-layer strategy was successfully applied in polyploid wheat, demonstrating its robustness and cross-species applicability. Our work establishes a versatile framework for functional allele engineering, offering a precise and broadly applicable route for crop improvement.

records.title: Discovery of an antagonist nanobody targeting the oxytocin receptor with tocolytic effect in mice.
records.abstract: Preterm birth, defined as delivery before 37 completed weeks of gestation, poses significant risks to maternal and neonatal health. These risks include neonatal respiratory distress syndrome, intraventricular hemorrhage, long-term developmental challenges, and in severe cases, mortality. Addressing these issues, G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR)-mediated tocolysis has become a focal strategy in pharmaceutical research to mitigate preterm labor risks. Most GPCR drugs are small molecules, yet their tendency to cross the placental barrier and induce fetal toxicity presents a significant challenge. Antibody drugs, with minimal cell membrane permeability, offer a promising alternative. In this study, we leverage AI-driven protein design to enable nanobody screening and identify several nanobodies with antagonist activity against the oxytocin receptor, a key target for preterm birth therapeutics. One of these nanobodies demonstrates antagonist activity comparable to Atosiban, a commonly used clinical drug, while exhibiting higher subtype selectivity. Pharmacological and structural analyses reveal mechanisms distinct from small molecule antagonists. These findings expand the pharmacological potential of antibody drugs and introduce useful tools and perspectives for developing effective tocolytic agents.

records.title: Integrated computation-guided thermostabilization of the fungal sweet protein Honey Truffle Sweetener.
records.abstract: Thermostability limits the use of sweet proteins as sugar substitutes in thermally processed foods. Here, we report an integrated computation-guided workflow for thermostabilizing Honey Truffle Sweetener (HTS), a recently identified fungal sweet protein with low intrinsic stability. We determined the HTS crystal structure and used it to guide subsequent computational analyses. Rosetta and ThermoMPNN evaluated candidate substitutions from complementary physics-based and deep-learning-based perspectives, and the selected single-mutant library was experimentally characterized. The resulting melting-temperature data were then used to develop SMRC-Net, which combines mutation-centered features from the ESM2 protein language model with molecular dynamics-derived structural descriptors to support mutation prioritization. Repeated nested cross-validation supported quantitative Tm prediction within the HTS scaffold, while prospective testing showed 9/10 directional agreement in a small, computationally selected variant set. Validated substitutions were then assembled stepwise in small modules, followed by the introduction of an engineered disulfide bond. The final variant, FM, had a melting temperature of 82.1 °C, 27.5 °C higher than that of wild-type HTS. Untreated FM retained sweetness, while separate heat- and pH-treatment assays showed retained solubility and largely preserved secondary-structure profiles. Sweetness after these treatments was not evaluated. Molecular dynamics analyses indicated that FM was not uniformly rigidified but instead exhibited localized flexibility redistribution and a more consolidated conformational ensemble. This work provides a practical computation-guided framework for protein thermostabilization, with potential applicability to other compact proteins.

records.title: Circulating tumor DNA as a liquid biopsy for glioma detection in cerebrospinal fluid and plasma: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
records.abstract: Accurate molecular characterization of gliomas is essential for determining prognosis and guiding therapeutic decisions. In recent years, liquid biopsy for analysis of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) in blood or cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) has emerged as a promising, minimally invasive alternative. This study evaluates the existing literature on the utility of ctDNA detection in CSF and blood in patients with gliomas, with the goal of assessing its ability to identify mutations concordant with those detected in tumor tissue. A systematic search was conducted up to April 30, 2026, to identify cohorts that evaluated the effectiveness of ctDNA-based liquid biopsies for gliomas. The primary assessed outcomes were the sensitivity and specificity of the liquid biopsies using CSF or plasma. A pooled sensitivity analysis was performed, as well as summary receiver operating characteristic (SROC) curves. Twenty-eight studies met the inclusion criteria, encompassing 613 patients. Meta-analysis of diagnostic performance revealed improved biomarker performance for CSF (Area under the curve [AUC] 0.95) ctDNA. Pooled sensitivity for ctDNA detection in patients with gliomas was higher in CSF 0.79 (95% CI, 0.69-0.85) than in plasma 0.29 (95% CI, 0.15-0.47), P < .0001. The literature demonstrates a promising performance of ctDNA analysis in patients with diffuse gliomas as a liquid biopsy strategy. CSF ctDNA analysis exhibited superior sensitivity compared to plasma ctDNA. This meta-analysis supports the utility of ctDNA, particularly CSF ctDNA, as a complementary diagnostic tool in neuro-oncology.

records.title: AI-driven multi-omics biomarkers in precision breast cancer therapeutics: from discovery to clinical translation.
records.abstract: Breast cancer is biologically heterogeneous, yet conventional clinical decisions rely on static, single-marker proxies (ER, PR, HER2, and Ki-67) that capture only a narrow slice of tumor biology. This mini-review argues that AI-driven multi-omics biomarkers offer a valuable shift toward systems-level, model-derived probabilities integrating genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic, and imaging information to explain and predict disease behavior more faithfully. We synthesize recent advances across three domains: (i) computational strategies for multi-omics integration, from classical penalized regression and ensemble learning to deep multimodal architectures and foundation-model embeddings; (ii) therapeutically relevant biomarker classes across tissue, liquid biopsy, and imaging modalities; and (iii) emerging pathways for embedding these biomarkers into clinical decision support. We highlight validation, interpretability, and robust handling of missing modalities as prerequisites for clinical trust, and outline how biomarker-driven trials, standardized reporting (e.g., TRIPOD + AI), and privacy-preserving data consortia can move AI-driven multi-omics biomarkers toward clinical and regulatory maturity.

records.title: Stromal or exosome derived lncRNAs regulate stemness in hepatocellular carcinoma.
records.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains one of the most prevalent malignancies worldwide, with high recurrence rates and chemotherapy resistance posing major clinical challenges. Cancer stem cells (CSCs) are recognized as an important contributors of HCC initiation, metastasis, and recurrence. Within the tumor microenvironment (TME), cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) can maintain CSC properties through intercellular communication. Exosomes serve as essential mediators of this process by delivering long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) from various TME cells (including CAFs, MSCs, macrophages, and HCC cells themselves) to recipient HCC cells. A literature search of PubMed and Web of Science Core Collection (inception to March 2026) was conducted using key terms including "HCC", "CAFs", "MSCs", "Macrophages", "Exosome", "LncRNA", and "Neoplastic Stem Cells". Studies were selected based on topic relevance and methodological rigor; those with incomplete or inaccessible data were excluded. The retrieved literature was synthesized to elucidate the mechanisms by which lncRNAs modulate downstream signaling pathways and to evaluate their translational potential as diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets. This review identifies multiple mechanisms through which stromal or exosome derived lncRNAs regulate HCC cell stemness, including YAP liquid-liquid phase separation, chromatin remodeling via recruitment of SWI/SNF, INO80, NuRD, and BRM/BRG1 complexes, Wnt/β-catenin pathway modulation through protein stabilization and competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) networks, STAT3 pathway regulation via direct transcriptional repression and transcription factor recruitment, and BMP signaling pathway engagement. Functional classification reveals that these lncRNAs converge on core stemness pathways through complementary transcriptional, posttranscriptional, and protein-level regulatory mechanisms, while integrating signals from the TME. Stromal or exosome derived lncRNAs constitute a critical regulatory layer in HCC stemness maintenance and hold significant promise as noninvasive diagnostic biomarkers via liquid biopsy. Antisense oligonucleotide (ASO)-based therapeutic strategies targeting the stromal cell-lncRNA-CSC axis represent a promising direction. Nevertheless, systematic characterization of stromal or exosome derived lncRNA species, elucidation of lncRNA sorting and uptake mechanisms, and clinical validation of biomarker and therapeutic applications remain important challenges for future investigation.

records.title: Correlation between circulating tumor cell levels and tumor response in patients with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma undergoing immunotherapy and molecular targeted therapy.
records.abstract: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) are closely associated with the progression of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, the clinical value of CTC detection in patients receiving systemic therapy for advanced HCC remains to be fully elucidated. A total of 125 patients with advanced HCC who underwent systemic therapy were enrolled in this study. Five milliliters of peripheral blood were collected at five time points: before treatment initiation, and 1 month, 3 months, 6 months, and 1 year after treatment. CTCs were isolated and captured using the Isolation by Size of Epithelial Tumor Cells (ISET) method. Tumor response to systemic treatment was evaluated according to the modified Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (mRECIST). We further analyzed the correlation between dynamic changes in peripheral blood CTC levels and tumor response to systemic therapy. The overall objective response rate (ORR) and disease control rate (DCR) were 39.2% (49/125) and 82.4% (103/125), respectively. Dynamic monitoring of CTCs revealed that CTC levels remained persistently high and gradually increased in patients with progressive disease (PD). In patients with complete response (CR) or partial response (PR), CTC levels decreased progressively during treatment and stayed at low levels thereafter. For patients with stable disease (SD), CTC counts began to decline 3 months after treatment but remained higher than those in patients with CR or PR. Baseline CTC levels were negatively correlated with treatment efficacy: patients with higher baseline CTC counts exhibited poorer tumor responses. Patients with baseline CTC counts < 15, CTC counts < 13 at 1 month post-treatment, and CTC counts < 10 at 3 months post-treatment were more likely to achieve an objective tumor response and obtained better therapeutic outcomes. Additionally, these patients had significantly longer progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) compared with those who exceeded the above cut-off values. Peripheral blood CTC counts are correlated with tumor treatment response in patients with advanced HCC. Serial CTC detection serves as a valuable tool for evaluating the efficacy of systemic therapy in advanced HCC.

records.title: Current applications and challenges of artificial intelligence in orthopedic imaging: A narrative review.
records.abstract: BackgroundArtificial intelligence (AI), especially machine and deep learning, is an emerging tool in medicine with growing applications in orthopedic imaging. Given imaging's central role in diagnosis, surgical planning, and treatment monitoring, this narrative review maps the current and potential uses of AI in orthopedics, identifies underdevelopment sections, and emphasizes limitations in clinical practice.MethodsA PubMed search used the terms "Orthopedic," "Imaging," and "Artificial Intelligence." Studies were screened by title and abstract, excluding non-orthopedic or non-AI studies, animal research, pediatric populations, and robotics or pharmacology papers. Eighty-five peer-reviewed articles were analyzed for imaging modality, clinical application, AI technique, and assigned a level of evidence. They were selected based on relevance to AI in orthopedic imaging.ResultsAI applications spanned radiography, CT, MRI, DTI, and ultrasound. For bone pathology, AI aided fracture detection and osteoarthritis prediction with clinician-level accuracy. In soft tissue injuries, models assisted in rotator cuff and meniscus tear detection and muscle segmentation. AI-driven 3D reconstructions and virtual reduction models enhanced surgical planning, particularly in joint replacement and trauma. Spine imaging benefited from vertebral segmentation, disc degeneration classification, and paraspinal muscle analysis, improving preoperative planning and outcome prediction. radiography, CT, MRI, DTI, and ultrasound. An important distinction is that many of these models generated outputs that surrounded conditional probabilities rather than categorical diagnoses. Many pitfalls remain including single-center overfitting, data leakage, and inter-reader variability.ConclusionsAI demonstrates potential to enhance diagnostic accuracy, streamline surgical planning, and improve workflow efficiency. Challenges remain, including data bias, regulatory constraints, and ethical considerations, warranting caution to its blanket application in medicine. Continued integration and validation are needed for optimal clinical use.Clinical RelevanceAI may serve as an adjunct to clinicians, supporting imaging interpretation and surgical decision-making while preserving human judgment.

records.title: Liquid biopsy in bladder cancer: towards precision oncology.
records.abstract: Bladder cancer (BC), as the most common form of urothelial carcinoma, represents a substantial global health burden owing to its high rates of late diagnosis and disease recurrence. Current standard diagnostics, such as cystoscopy and tissue biopsy, are invasive, costly, and limited in capturing tumor heterogeneity or enabling longitudinal monitoring. These constraints underscore the urgent need for minimally invasive, reliable biomarkers. Over the past decade, liquid biopsy has emerged as a transformative, non-invasive alternative, enabling the dynamic profiling of circulating tumor-derived components like circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), circulating tumor cells (CTC), and extracellular vesicles (EVs). This review comprehensively synthesizes the role of these liquid biopsy analytes in advancing the early detection, prognostic stratification, treatment response monitoring, and immunophenotyping of Urothelial Carcinoma(UC). We critically evaluate the underlying technological advances, consolidate key clinical evidence, discuss persisting challenges, and outline the translational path toward integrating liquid biopsy into precision oncology paradigms for BC management.
